newsitem.title: USA: Georgia economic indicators surge upward in April.
newsitem.headline: Georgia economic indicators surge upward in April.

text.p: Georgia's Composite Index of Leading Economic Indicators surged upward in April, registering its biggest gain in 14 months, state Labor Commissioner David Poythress said in his monthly report.
Leaading indicators, designed to forecast economic activity three to six months ahead, rose 2.22 points in April to 149.44 on a 1988 base of 100.
The state's Composite Index of Coincident Indicators, designed to measure current conditions, rose 1.45 points in April to 146.71 on a 1987 base of 100.

Upward momentum in the leading index was fueled by sharp increases in residential construction, motor vehicle sales and the length of the manufacturing workweek, and by a decline in unemployment claims.
Local governments issued 6,843 permits for housing construction in April, up from 6,187 in March and 5,672 in February.
The state issued 45,403 titles for new motor vehicles in April, up from 38,505 in March.
Georgia's average manufacturing workweek increased by 30 minutes, to 42.7 hors in April. It was the longest workweek since 42.9 hours were recorded in January of 1995.
The gain suggests pending growth in manufacturing employment, which increased by 500 to 588,700 in April.
Average weekly manufacturing earnings rose $2.48 in April to $494.32, partly due to increased overtime hours.
Initial unemployment claims dropped by 2.82 percent in April to 26,764 while continuing unemployment claims dropped by 7.35 percent during the month to 166,656.
The stae's unemployment rate declined to 4.3 percent in April from 4.7 percent in March and 4.6 percent a year ago.
Total nonfarm employment grew by 6,000 to 3.58 million during the month. For the year, the employment total rose by 72,000, or 2.05 percent over the record level recorded in April of 1996.
New corporate charters and total revenue collections were the only slow spots for the month.

The state issued 3,103 applications for new corporate charters, down from 3,149 in March. Revenue collections declined to $865.9 million in April from $870 million in March. Sales tax receipts dipped to $334.7 million in April from $347.3 million in March.
